headline: Remote Arctic Access and Mandatory Visitor Registration
reservation: All visitors must register with Parks Canada and attend a mandatory polar bear safety briefing before entering the park. Accommodation at the Torngat Mountains Base Camp and Research Station is managed separately from park entry and requires advance booking; systems for charter flights and vessel transfers change annually and require direct confirmation with official providers.

days.title: Fiords and Inuit Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Torngat Mountains Base Camp

stops.name: Saglek Fiord
stops.detail: Observe the dramatic vertical rock faces and look for marine wildlife from a boat-based perspective.

stops.name: Sallikuluk (Rose Island)
stops.detail: Visit this cultural landscape featuring ancient Inuit burial sites and traditional sod house remains with a local guide.

days.driving: Allow 4–6 hours for boat transfers; conditions vary by sea state
days.note: Weather in the North Atlantic can cause sudden travel delays or cancellations.

days.title: Glacial Valleys and Tundra
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Base Camp dock

stops.name: Ramah Bay
stops.detail: Explore the site of a former Moravian mission and the unique translucent Ramah chert used historically for tools.

stops.name: Nakvak Brook
stops.detail: Hike the valley floor to witness the intersection of jagged peaks and arctic tundra flora.

days.driving: Predominantly water-based transport; hiking time varies by group pace
days.note: Wildlife monitors are required for all shore excursions due to polar bear activity.

days.title: Northern Fiords and Ice Fields

stops.name: Nachvak Fiord
stops.detail: Travel deep into the park's interior where the highest peaks of the Torngat Mountains dominate the skyline.

stops.name: Komaktorvik River
stops.detail: View the rugged river system that serves as a gateway to the park's northern wilderness.

days.driving: Allow for a full day of mixed marine and foot travel; conditions vary
days.note: July and August offer the only reliable window for interior fiord access.

intel.title: Airside Staging
intel.text: There are no public roads or parking lots in the park; vehicles are staged at the gateway airports in Nain or Kuujjuaq. Confirm secure storage with local air charter providers before arrival.

intel.title: Satellite Dependency
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent within the park boundaries. Satellite phones or GPS messengers are standard requirements for all independent parties.

intel.title: Base Camp Supplies
intel.text: Fuel is not available for purchase within the park; all supplies are managed through the Torngat Mountains Base Camp. Expeditions must carry all necessary reserves for the duration of their trip.

intel.title: Ice Break-up
intel.text: Access is strictly limited by the timing of sea ice break-up, typically occurring in mid-to-late July. Earlier attempts are often blocked by pack ice in Saglek Bay.

intel.title: Mandatory Bear Monitors
intel.text: Parks Canada requires visitors to be accompanied by a trained polar bear monitor. Solo hiking without professional protection is highly discouraged and often restricted.

plan.arrival: Upon arrival at Nain or Kuujjuaq, transfer to your pre-arranged charter flight; ensure all supplies are purchased in the gateway town before the final leg.
plan.vehicle: No road access; travel is exclusively by boat, aircraft, or on foot. Verify luggage weight limits with charter airlines.
plan.goldenHour: The cliffs of Saglek Fiord offer exceptional light during the late summer midnight sun, though fog can obscure views at any time.
